Title: Libri symbolici Ecclesiae Orientalis: Gennadii Confessiones; Cyrilli Lucaris Confessio; Orthodoxa Confessio (Petri Mogilae); Synodus Hierosolymitana (Dosithei), Greek and Latin in parallel columns, with prolegomena
Creator: Gennadius Scholarius, Cyril Lucaris, Peter Mogila (the Orthodox Confession) and the Synod of Jerusalem of 1672 under Dositheus; edited by Ernst Julius Kimmel (1812-1846)
Publisher: Jena: apud Carolum Hochhausenium
Publication Date: 1843 (title page 'MDCCCXLIII', read 'MDCCCXLIIIL.' in the OCR at file line 323)
Rights: Public Domain (published 1843, more than 95 years before 2026; Internet Archive possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT)
Language: grc
Source: Internet Archive item librisymbolicie00kimmgoog, file librisymbolicie00kimmgoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly (curl, raw bytes) by the library/source-research thread (Era VII session, second pass, VI.17 world agent), 2026-10-23; host rights statement: possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT; Google Books scan (id uLx0XZkBQCgC) of the Harvard University copy; the 1843 imprint is read on the title page in the OCR
Provenance note: Header prepended; the OCR text follows unchanged (no characters altered, nothing retyped, dropped or corrected; the file contains 0 long-s glyphs; the OCR's doubled spaces between words are left as scanned). Rights basis restated: a book printed at Jena in 1843 is public domain in the United States by date under the 95-year rule. File line numbers cited in this header are counted in the OCR text alone, before this header: add 10 to find a cited line in this file.
Content note: Language tag 'grc' for the Greek column; the Latin column and Kimmel's prolegomena (PROLEGOMENA at file line 206, with a life of Gennadius, an account of the Lucaris confession's editions and the history of each text) are Latin. Order in the file: Google Books boilerplate, title pages, prolegomena, then the texts with running heads: Gennadii Confessio I (from file line 4543) and II (from about file line 6244), Cyrilli Lucaris Confessio (about file lines 8754 to 8900), Orthodoxa Confessio (the Mogila confession, from about file line 8905 to about file line 40100), Synodus Hierosolymitana (the Jerusalem acts and Dositheus's confession, from about file line 40187 to about file line 59760), then indexes. This is the 1843 first printing of the collection that the vendored Kimmel 1850 (monumenta-fidei-ecclesiae-orientalis_confessions-grc-lat_kimmel1850.txt) enlarged; the texts are the same. It is vendored as a second scan of the Greek: at the sampled points the Greek column here is read whole where the 1850 scan's OCR cuts the column (compare 'Πρόγνωσις, προορισμὸς καὶ πρόνοια εἶναι διαφορετικαῖς ἐνεργείαις' here with the broken reading in the 1850 file), though it holds fewer Greek letters overall (about 338,000 against 436,000). OCR sampled at five points: the Latin clean, the Greek polytonic and readable at the sampled points with scattered misreads (ϑ for θ, Latin letters inside Greek words); check every quotation against the page images.

Quaestio XXIV. 
Quid est superbia ? 


Resp. Superbia est in- 
ordinata et injusta gloriae 
suae ambitio, ut super alios 
sibi aequales, qua jure qua 
injria, emineat. Hoc pec- 
catum omnium primum erat, 
quod in Lucifero exorieba- 
tur; ex quo, velut ex suf- 
fusa veneno scaturigine, ce- 
tera omnia promanarunt. De 
eo sic ait Sapientia (Pro- 
verb. VIII, 13.): Timor Do- 


mini odit injustitiam et in- 


juriam et superbiam et vias 


improborum. Et alibi Scri- 
ptura (Sirach. X, 7.): Odi- 
osa coram Domino et ho- 


minibus est superbia. Huic . 


vitio contraria humilitatis vir- 
tus est, quam Dominus no- 
ster lesus Christus com- 
mendans, nosque ad illam 
amplectendam adhortans, sic 
loquitur (Matth. XI, 29.): 
Discite a me, quod mitis 
sum, et humilis corde, et 
invenietis requiem animabus 
vestris.
